drills.title: Build the loading screen
drills.prompt: Put the lines in order so the program prints the goal output. Two lines do not belong.
drills.explain: A program runs top to bottom, so the order of the print lines is the order of the output. end="..." keeps the next print on the same line. Python is case-sensitive (Print is not print) and arguments are separated by commas.

drills.title: Separator and ending
drills.prompt: Fill the two blanks so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: sep sets what goes between the items of one print. end sets what is printed after it (a new line by default), so end="..." lets the next print continue on the same line.

drills.title: Text or number?
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: In quotes, 2 + 3 is just text and is shown as written. Without quotes Python does the maths and shows 5. sep goes between the items, and \n starts a new line.

drills.title: Case matters
drills.prompt: This program stops with a NameError. Click the line that causes it, then choose the right fix.
drills.explain: Python is case-sensitive: print is a built-in, Print does not exist, so Python reports NameError and shows the line number in the traceback. Read the last line of the traceback first.

drills.title: Review the AI's receipt printer
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this receipt printer. It runs, but tick the statements that point at real problems.
code: # Cafe receipt (written by an AI assistant)

issues.text: Line 6 prints the text 30 + 50, not the sum 80
issues.why: Inside quotes 30 + 50 is plain text. Write print(30 + 50) (or print("Total:", 30 + 50)) to get 80.

issues.text: The prices are typed again in the total, so they can drift apart
issues.why: If a price changes, the item line and the total can disagree. Store each price once (a variable) and reuse it.

non_issues.text: sep=" Rs " is not allowed in print()
non_issues.why: sep accepts any text. It is placed between the items, giving Masala chai Rs 30.

non_issues.text: The comment on line 1 will appear on the receipt
non_issues.why: Python ignores everything after # when it runs, so comments are never printed.

non_issues.text: print("Chai Point") should be written with a capital P
non_issues.why: print is lower case. A capital P (Print) would raise a NameError.

drills.explain: Reviewing AI code means asking: does it print what it claims, and will it stay correct when something changes? Here the quotes turn a calculation into text, and the repeated prices are a maintenance trap.
